title: CORS reflects any origin and allows credentials
summary: The site echoes whatever Origin a request carries into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true. That lets any other website make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, so a malicious page a signed-in user visits can read their data from this site.

confirm.control: A normal request without the foreign Origin, so the reflected origin stands out as a reflection, not the site's own policy.

reproduce: curl -sk -i 'https://host/' -H 'Origin: https://canary-cors.example' and check the response: Access-Control-Allow-Origin comes back as https://canary-cors.example and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is true. Reflecting an arbitrary origin with credentials means any site can read a signed-in user's data cross-origin.
remediate: Do not reflect the Origin header. Allow credentials only for an explicit allow list of trusted origins, and never combine Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true with an origin the request supplied or with a wildcard.
